name: Junction box plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a junction or joint box where installation cables are connected or branched.
description: A junction box mark shows where cables are joined in an enclosure, commonly in ceiling voids for lighting circuits or above ceilings for equipment connections. Plans draw a small circle or square with a dot, sometimes labelled JB, at the location.

Access matters: joints must remain accessible for inspection unless a maintenance-free method is used, so the plan should not place a junction box above a fixed plasterboard ceiling without an access panel. The symbol helps coordinate this with architectural trades.
The mark does not show the number of terminals or cables. A junction box serving fixed equipment may also be a final connection point; check the schedule.
readingNotes: Check access to the box above fixed ceilings.
Look for the equipment it serves.
distinction: A conductor junction dot on a schematic shows electrical connection; this plan mark shows a physical box.
